title: Build an animated Astro station and measure its rendering cost
context: The owner requested station crew with walking/running/pointing and landmark travel, Stålheart, Hugin, the antenna array and FPS comparisons in Astro.
outcome: Astro defaults to nine independently animated astronaut/scientist/worker crew, game-detail Stålheart and Hugin, the seven-dish SKYWARD array and MÖRK. Six self-contained GLBs are pinned to upstream b22a8c9a6e04d40819b68859624f362d6bff8680 with credits and clip/hash validation. Crew use authored animation crossfades and metre-per-second gait speeds with a pure visibility-graph route solver around expanded prop footprints. Landmark cycles play through preserved pivots. The scene supports 0–60 crew, per-group visibility, animation pause, clip auditions, camera focus, shadow/bloom toggles and portable scene links. Bounded local FPS/frame-time/p95/CPU-submit samples, whole-frame draw/triangle counters and per-group mesh budgets support a baseline comparison. Legacy astronaut studies load lazily and stay separate; gameplay assets/presets are unchanged.
alternatives: The original one-metre grid produced distracting aliasing across the larger yard; the station uses a fainter five-metre grid.
No per-object GPU-time claim: group rows report visible mesh budgets before extra passes, and CPU/submission duration is labelled separately.
Crew instances share geometry/materials and own skeletons/mixers; rebuilding the population releases old skeleton textures.
evidence: npm run check and build passed; pinned asset hashes and authored clips validated
npm run test:browser: full source acceptance passed

node scripts/browser-test.mjs --dist --astro passed: six assets, role/clip variety, movement, landmark cycles, pause, group exclusion, count changes, released skeleton textures, shared URL settings and disposal
